2.role: tip + the one casual app mention
2.asset: sheet music, notebook, open case, tuner on a stand, no app UI

A: intonation is SO important you guys, and it's really easy to not notice
check your notes against a drone or a tuner while you practice! i use this app called {app}, it tells me exactly which notes i got wrong
B: your open strings are a free tuner and nobody uses them 🥹
3rd finger in first position is an octave above the string below, check it every single time!! i also run {app} while i practice so it flags whatever i miss
C: turn the vibrato OFF when you're checking intonation
vibrato hides a flat note from you AND from a tuner lol. i practice the passage plain first then check it with {app} before adding it back in
D: record yourself. you will be humbled 😭
your ears genuinely lie to you while you're playing!! voice memos work fine honestly, i use {app} because it marks the bits that went wrong so i don't have to sit there relistening to everything
E: play QUIETER when something isn't in tune
you hear so much more at a soft dynamic, it's kind of magic. that plus a drone fixed more for me than any amount of scales (i check mine with {app} now)
F: stop starting from the top every single time!!
your first 8 bars are amazing and your ending is a mess, be honest 🥲 pick the bar that's actually broken. {app} tells me which one that is if i can't tell
G: private teachers are SO expensive and i need you to know that's okay!!
you can get really far on your own i promise 🥹 free stuff first: a tuner, a drone track, and recording yourself. i also use this app called {app} because it tells me exactly which notes i got wrong
H: there were no violin teachers near me and i almost didn't start 😭
so glad i did anyway!! it's just youtube, a metronome and {app} for me, it listens while i play and catches the notes i can't hear are off. genuinely so doable on your own 💕

3.role: ear and intonation, no app mention
3.asset: fingerboard, strings, tuner, hand in position

A: hear the note in your head BEFORE you put the finger down ✨
not even joking this one genuinely changed my playing more than anything else on this list. sing it in your head first, THEN go find it with your finger
B: a perfect 5th rings when it's in tune 🎻
if you hear kind of a wobble in the sound that's literally just the two notes fighting each other, keep adjusting till it smooths out
C: practise with a drone!! it's so humbling but so good
just hold a note against it and let it settle, you'll start hearing the problem before the tuner even tells you
D: i know, i know. but you're using your eyes for something your ears should be doing. feels awful for like two weeks and then your ear just takes over i promise
E: play slow enough that you can actually hear each note land
if it's too fast for you to hear it's too fast to fix tbh. speed is always the last thing you add, never the first
F: sing the phrase before you play it
you'll be shocked how much cleaner it comes out honestly. your fingers are just following your ear this whole time, not the other way around

4.role: bow, vibrato, posture, no app mention
4.asset: bow hold, right arm mid-stroke, shoulder and chin frame

A: a straight bow isn't a straight arm 🤯
your hand actually travels in a slight curve, out towards the tip and back in towards the frog. that's the whole secret to keeping the bow parallel to the bridge
B: loudness comes from bow SPEED, not pressure
pressing harder just chokes the string honestly, try moving faster and a little closer to the bridge instead
C: your contact point changes the whole sound 🎻
near the bridge is loud and bright, near the fingerboard is soft and airy. just pick one on purpose instead of drifting around
D: if your thumb is squeezing, your vibrato is dead ✨
it's the number one thing killing it honestly. you should be able to wiggle your thumb loose mid note, if you can't you're gripping too hard
E: slow wide vibrato first, speed comes later 🥹
metronome at 60, two swings per beat. it narrows on its own as it speeds up so don't go chasing fast right away
F: long tones on one open string. that's the whole warmup.
whole bow, as slow as you can possibly hold it steady. so boring honestly but it fixes more than any étude ever will

5.asset: music stand, practice space, notebook, metronome

A: when you practice focus on one spot at a time! wandering around without a plan just means you're rehearsing your mistakes over and over
B: practise the hard bar, not the whole piece 🥹
four bars, fifty times, slowly, that's a real session. running it top to bottom over and over is honestly just performing at yourself lol
C: slow, then medium, then fast. don't skip the middle one.
if it falls apart at tempo you skipped a step somewhere. going back down feels like losing but it genuinely isn't
D: a little every day beats one long weekend session 🎻
your hands genuinely learn stuff overnight while you sleep. fifteen minutes daily will straight up outrun two hours on a sunday
E: picking something way too hard feels ambitious but honestly it mostly just teaches you tension. the piece that's one step up is the one that actually makes you better
F: stop the second you feel your hand tense up
tension is honestly the fastest way to build a habit you'll spend a whole year undoing. just shake it out, breathe, and start again
